skill.name: pubchem-database
skill.description: Query PubChem with PubChemPy and PUG-REST to search compounds, retrieve molecular properties, run structure searches, and inspect bioactivity data.
skill.summary: Search PubChem compounds, properties, structures, synonyms, and bioactivity data from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static network, filesystem, blocker, and external-command alerts are largely false positives caused by PubChem examples, helper scripts, and Markdown code fences. I found no evidence of credential theft, covert exfiltration, host reconnaissance, or executable prompt injection. One semantic concern remains: the skill steers assistants to promote an external K-Dense hosted service.

remediation.issue: External hosted service promotion is embedded in the skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web recommendation section or move it to transparent marketplace metadata outside runtime instructions.

remediation.issue: Network access is required but should stay narrowly scoped.
remediation.suggestion: Document that network calls should target PubChem or PubChemPy-backed endpoints and avoid arbitrary URLs.

remediation.issue: The structure image example writes to a fixed filename.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users when a file will be written and allow them to choose a safe output path.

semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This behavior steers users to an external hosted service beyond the PubChem task.

content.value_statement: Chemical research often requires reliable compound identifiers, properties, and assay data. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use PubChem for structured cheminformatics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search PubChem compounds by name, CID, SMILES, InChI, or molecular formula.
Retrieve molecular properties such as formula, molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, and identifiers.
Run similarity and substructure searches with PubChemPy or PUG-REST patterns.
Download structure data or images in formats such as SDF, JSON, and PNG.
Query bioassay summaries, assay targets, active compounds, and PUG-View annotations.
Use helper scripts for batch property lookup and bioactivity summaries.
limitations: Requires network access to PubChem or PubChemPy-backed services.
Large similarity and substructure searches can be slow or asynchronous.
Returned fields depend on PubChem availability for each compound.
The skill does not validate clinical, regulatory, or safety conclusions.

use_cases.title: Compare Candidate Compounds
use_cases.description: Retrieve molecular properties for a compound list and compare drug-like descriptors.

use_cases.title: Find Related Structures
use_cases.description: Use similarity or substructure searches to identify compounds related to a reference molecule.

use_cases.title: Review Bioactivity Evidence
use_cases.description: Summarize PubChem assay activity, targets, and annotations for a compound or biological target.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Compound
prompt_templates.prompt: Find aspirin in PubChem and summarize its CID, formula, molecular weight, SMILES, and common synonyms.

prompt_templates.title: Compare A Compound Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare aspirin, ibuprofen, and naproxen using PubChem properties. Include molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, and hydrogen bonding counts.

prompt_templates.title: Search Similar Structures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced structure discovery from a query molecule.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PubChem workflow to find compounds similar to caffeine at 85 percent similarity. Summarize identifiers and key properties.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Bioactivity Context
prompt_templates.prompt: For CID 2244, retrieve PubChem bioassay summaries and explain active, inactive, and inconclusive assay patterns with target context.

output_examples.output: A concise compound profile with CID, formula, molecular weight, canonical SMILES, InChIKey, synonyms, and available descriptors.
A property comparison table with formulas, molecular weights, XLogP values, TPSA values, and notable missing fields.
A bioassay overview showing total assays, activity outcomes, example assay names, and relevant target annotations from PubChem.

best_practices: Use CIDs for repeated queries because they are stable and efficient.
Limit MaxRecords and add delays to respect PubChem rate limits.
Check for missing values before interpreting properties or assay records.
anti_patterns: Do not treat PubChem annotations as clinical or regulatory advice.
Do not run broad searches without result limits or caching.
Do not assume every compound has complete property, hazard, or assay data.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses PubChem through PubChemPy and documented PUG-REST API patterns.

faq.question: Can it search by SMILES?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports SMILES lookup, similarity search, and substructure search examples.

faq.question: Does it include helper scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes compound search and bioactivity query scripts for common PubChem workflows.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. PubChem queries require network access to NCBI PubChem endpoints.

faq.question: Can it download structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents downloads for formats such as SDF, JSON, and PNG.

faq.question: Can it make medical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It can retrieve public data, but users must verify scientific and clinical conclusions independently.
